original_question: Clarify the relationship between flat virtual-knot theories and theories of doodles, including doodles with virtual crossings, and determine the resulting structures for cobordism, associated groups, and free-abelian cobordism classes of immersed surfaces without triple points.
target_in_paper: Section 8.1, Problem 4, "Virtuals and the theory of doodles" (page 28). This is the exact nearby open problem your draft is trying to capture, not the later general virtual-knot-cobordism questions in Section 8.2. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s intended comparison between flat virtual-knot theory and doodle theory, the idea of allowing virtual crossings in the doodle setting, and the cobordism theme involving immersed surfaces without triple points whose cobordism classes lie in a free abelian group. It also points toward the group-theoretic side of the problem. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))
missing_details: A doodle is not just any flat object: in the paper it is represented by a flat diagram in the plane, with Reidemeister moves of type I and II allowed but not type III; equivalently, triple points are excluded. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))

The flat side of the comparison should be stated using the paper’s definition of flat virtual theory: diagrams with flat crossings and virtual crossings, considered modulo generalized flat Reidemeister moves, with detour moves available for virtual crossings. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))

The paper’s official wording is to compare flat virtual-knot theories with theories of doodles; your phrase "determine the resulting structures" is broader and stronger than the stated problem, which is exploratory rather than a request for a complete structure theorem. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))

The draft omits two pieces of nearby paper-faithful context explicitly named in Problem 4: Khovanov’s group associated to doodles and the possibility of associating commutator identities to a doodle. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))

If virtual crossings are added, the paper interprets this as giving doodles on a surface of higher genus; that geometric higher-genus viewpoint should be stated explicitly in a stand-alone question. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))

For cobordism, the stand-alone question should say that the cobordism is by immersed surfaces without triple points, and that the cobordism classes represent elements of a free abelian group; the paper does not specify a presentation of that group, so one should not add extra algebraic structure beyond this. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))

A nearby remark also clarifies why doodles differ from ordinary knot-type theories: for doodle invariants one should not expect the Yang-Baxter condition, reflecting the absence of the type III move. This is implicit background missing from the draft. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))

There are no paper-critical parameters here involving an ambient ring or field, variables, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or quantifiers such as "for all sufficiently large m"; those generic items are simply not applicable to this problem. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))
refined_question: How can one compare flat virtual-knot theory—where one studies flat virtual diagrams with flat and virtual crossings modulo the generalized flat Reidemeister moves and detour moves—with doodle theory, where a doodle is a flat diagram in the plane modulo Reidemeister moves of types I and II but not III; and, after allowing virtual crossings as well as flat crossings so as to obtain doodles on surfaces of higher genus, how do the basic doodle structures mentioned in the paper, namely Khovanov’s associated group, commutator identities, and doodle cobordism by immersed surfaces without triple points whose cobordism classes lie in a free abelian group, extend or correspond in this virtualized setting? ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))
justification: The draft is clearly targeting Section 8.1, Problem 4 because it reproduces almost all of that paragraph’s distinctive content: flat virtual theories, doodles, virtual crossings, a doodle group, commutator identities, cobordism by immersed surfaces without triple points, and free-abelian cobordism classes. The nearby context in Section 2.2 supplies the precise flat-virtual side of the comparison, Section 2.3 supplies the higher-genus surface interpretation associated with virtual crossings, and the remark in Section 6.1 explains an implicit structural difference between doodles and ordinary knot-type theories by noting that doodle invariants should not be expected to satisfy the Yang-Baxter condition. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/86155))
